correctness.rationale: For k>=2 antichain layers the chain polytope is a coordinatewise downward-closed intersection of chain inequalities, so the farthest order point is the unique all-ones vertex. Permuting coordinates inside each layer reduces its Euclidean projection to strictly convex water filling with t_i=(1-lambda/m_i)_+ and sum_i t_i=1. Reverse squared distance maximizes at an antichain vertex, whose order-polytope isotonic projection pools a selected layer subset of size a with U_i higher coordinates, giving a U_i/(a+U_i). Strict monotonicity in a yields the stated max over full layers; two-layer equality and strict k>=3 forward dominance follow from the quadratic comparison, and k=1 is handled separately. Independent exact/rational water-filling calculations yielded (1,2,3): (h(O,C)^2,h(C,O)^2)=(11/5,6/5), reversed (3,2,1):(11/5,3/2), equal unit layers k=3:(4/3,2/3), k=4:(9/4,3/4). These sample tests corroborate the unrestricted convex proof, not replace it.
